name: Shader Development Studio
stack: three.js (WebGPURenderer and WebGLRenderer both in the bundle)
STIX Two Text self-hosted variable woff2 (next/font, weight 400-700)
techniques: whole site rendered to one canvas element
retro CRT boot screen as the loader (progress bar, version line, copyright line)
CRT vignette, chromatic fringe and scanline grain over the canvas
hidden DOM and ARIA layer behind the 3D graphics for assistive technology
custom keyboard navigation through the 3D space
project carousel as the Selected Work section
corporate-satire copy voice
accessibility statement written in the same voice, admitting the limits
palette: loader: one blue ground (about #3a3aa8 as rendered) with white and pale-yellow bitmap text, black CRT surround; Awwwards lists the site palette as #000000
type: STIX Two Text (serif, self-hosted, the only webfont in the CSS); the loader draws a serif italic SHADER wordmark and a bitmap monospace face on the canvas
motion: segmented progress bar filling during boot; Lenis smooth scroll and three.js scene once loaded (not observed in the headless render, which showed the loader at 1440 and 390 in both normal and reduced motion)
why: Awwwards Site of the Day 20 April 2026 (7.73, DEV 8.12 with Animations 9.40 and Accessibility 7.40), credited to Shader and Andreas Antonsson; tags Retro, Storytelling, 3D, 404 pages, next.js, WebGL, Three.js, React. Rendered here with webdesign.mjs debug: at 1440 and 390, normal and reduced motion, the page showed its loader - a CRT boot screen in one blue with a striped-globe mark, an italic serif SHADER wordmark, 'Shader Development Studio, Website / Version 1.02', a segmented progress bar and 'Copyright (c) Shader Development Studio AB, 2026' ('Shader Sweden AB' at 390). Everything past the loader is read from the served HTML and the bundle, not seen. What makes it good and not AI-looking: the 3D is authored for the subject - a development studio staging its own corporate site as an operating system booting on an old monitor is a joke only this company could make, not a hero that could front anything; restraint - one colour, one wordmark, one progress bar, no gradient, no cards, no icon grid; copy that names concrete things - Norrkoping, Blender, React Three Fiber, 8th Wall, Scenkonst Ost, 'Version 1.02', 'We don't troubleshoot printers', 'Scroll to Inspect Our Closed Deals'; sequencing - boot screen, then one continuous canvas (the accessibility statement says the whole enterprise is on a single canvas element with a hidden DOM and ARIA layer and custom keyboard navigation behind it), then a project carousel, the studio text, and a cal.com booking; sound - an AudioContext is in the bundle, but whether the site plays sound was not observed. The accessibility statement is written in the same shoulder-pads voice and says plainly that the canvas 'might not be 100 percent seamless for everyone', which is a human admission no template writes. Studio in Norrkoping, Sweden; the booking link on the page is Filip Kantedal's. Founding year and founders (2021, Simon Hedlund and Filip Kantedal, per a Norrkoping Science Park article surfaced by search) are UNVERIFIED here.
